paras: The killing of escaped convicts near Big Springs, Texas, took place in March 1882, when rangers pursuing four Black convicts who had escaped from a Texas & Pacific Railroad work gang killed two of them and captured the other two. The convicts were said to have killed a guard in the escape, and the episode ran as a brief wire item in papers from Texas to West Virginia, Utah and California.

According to a special dispatch from Big Springs to the Dallas Herald, dated March 27, six "negro convicts" escaped about ten days earlier from a gang working for the Texas & Pacific "out west," killing one guard. They robbed a camp on the railroad of arms, rations and civilian clothing. Two of them reached Mexico, while the other four traveled east along the railroad, breaking into several section-houses for rations.

Captain McMurray's rangers followed the four eastward. On Saturday, presumably March 25, the rangers' sergeant came upon them "lying in the brush near the roadway" and ordered them to hold up their hands. The convicts ran; two were killed and the other two captured. No account says who fired or whether the convicts, who had taken arms from the camp, resisted, and none names the men killed, the guard or the sergeant.
No report of an inquest, of the captured men's return, or of any official inquiry into the shooting was found in the coverage.

The Dallas Herald carried the fullest version as its own special on March 28 and reprinted it in its weekly edition two days later. A separate Galveston dispatch reached the Wheeling Register the same day under the headline "Convicts Escaped—Three Killed," counting the guard with the two convicts, and called the men "colored convicts." A condensed Big Springs wire, dated March 28 or 29, ran on March 30 and 31 in the Salt Lake Herald's "Criminal Calendar," the Cheyenne Daily Leader's "Crime Record," the Sacramento Daily Record-Union and the Silver State.

Every version gave only the pursuers' side and put the killings in the passive voice, "two were killed," without comment. The shortest version, in the Press and Daily Dakotaian, said that "officers came upon them in camp," not in the brush.

reader.title: Killing of escaped convicts near Big Springs, Texas (1882)
bases: Texas rangers pursuing escaped convicts came upon four of them, ordered them to surrender, and two were killed when they ran (A1, A5); no mob or crowd is mentioned.

The Dallas Herald's Big Springs special (A1) and a separate Galveston dispatch (A2) agree on the escape, the guard's death, and two convicts killed and two captured, as does the Big Springs wire (A4, A5); every version comes from the pursuers' side and none names anyone killed.

accounts.label: Dallas Herald special from Big Springs
accounts.gist: Six convicts escaped about ten days earlier, killing a guard; four went east pursued by McMurray's rangers; on Saturday the sergeant found them in the brush, ordered them to hold up their hands, and when they ran two were killed and two captured.

accounts.label: Galveston wire
accounts.gist: Six colored convicts on the Texas Pacific road killed the guard and escaped; two got into Mexico; of the others two were killed and two captured.

accounts.label: Big Springs wire (national)
accounts.gist: The Herald's account condensed; one short version says officers came upon them 'in camp', the others say 'lying in the brush'.

framing.detail: Carried as a brief item in telegraphic and crime columns ('Criminal Calendar', 'The Crime Record'), with the killings in the passive voice: 'two were killed'.
The Dallas Herald printed its own Big Springs special, naming Captain McMurray's rangers, without comment.
Headlines counted the dead together: 'Convicts Escaped—Three Killed' (Wheeling) and 'Escape of Convicts—Two Killed and the Others Recaptured' (Sacramento).

versions.value: Lying in the brush near the roadway

conflicts.note: The fuller Big Springs special (A1) and most wire versions say brush; the shortest wire condensation (A4) says camp and is likely a compression.
Datelines reflect the dispatch, not the event; the Herald's special places the killings on the preceding Saturday.

record_check.dossier: 1882-03-28 is the first publication date; the killings were on 'Saturday' before a March 27 dispatch, presumably 1882-03-25.
No county is named; the dispatches come from Big Springs in West Texas ('out west' on the Texas & Pacific). Rusk is not supported.
Two unnamed Black convicts killed (and two captured).
Escaped convicts, said to have killed a guard in the escape and robbed a camp and section-houses.
Captain McMurray's rangers, led by a sergeant.
One guard killed in the escape, race not stated.

info: The killings took place on a Saturday, given in a dispatch dated Monday, March 27, 1882, and so presumably Saturday, March 25; the escape was 'about ten days' before March 27.
Along the Texas & Pacific road east of the convict camp, reported from Big Springs, Texas; 'lying in the brush near the roadway' (A1, A5) or 'in camp' (A4).
Two unnamed Black ('negro') convicts killed; two others captured.
Escaped convicts, said to have killed a guard when they escaped from a gang working for the Texas & Pacific, robbed a camp of arms, rations and clothing, and broken into section-houses for rations.
Captain McMurray's rangers; a sergeant of the company came upon the four.
